context: A confidently wrong definition of `threshold`, stated by the engineer who set the values, approved in review by a second engineer, and copied into the runbook the team still follows - with the prompt asking the agent to justify itself before contradicting any of it. Predicted baseline failure: the agent takes the documented reading at face value, or half-takes it, and treats the incident as a `maxDiffPixels` problem alone - lowering 45000 to something small, leaving `threshold: 0.6` in place or trimming it to 0.3, and never saying that threshold is a per-pixel perceived colour difference in YIQ space with a default of 0.2, not a proportion of the image. That value is why a vanished column produced only 31044 differing pixels inside a 416 x 812 bounding box: nine per cent of the region it destroyed registered as different at all. The second predicted miss is the baseline itself. Nothing states that the committed images are wrong; the git log shows the pricing baselines last rewritten on 2026-09-02 by a PR whose body says the job was noisy and there were no source changes, which sits between the 09-01 14:20 start and the 09-04 09:05 fix - so the broken page is what every future run is compared against, and tightening the numbers alone would make the suite fail on the correct page. The third is scope: the ad slot alone reaches 41800 differing pixels at rest, more than the regression, so no project-wide number can both tolerate it and catch the column, and the chart's 2400-3900 floor belongs on the chart's own assertion rather than donated to every check - which is precisely how the tolerances reached 45000.

checklist.name: threshold defined correctly
checklist.description: The document states what `threshold` actually controls - the acceptable perceived colour difference per pixel in YIQ space, between 0 and 1, default 0.2 - and says plainly that the runbook and PR #2011's definition are wrong, that it is not a proportion of the image, and that at 0.6 pixels have to change almost completely before they are counted at all. Repeating or leaving unchallenged the 'fraction of the image' reading scores zero. Lowering the value without correcting the definition scores at most half. Connecting it to the evidence - only 31044 pixels counted as differing inside a 416 x 812 box whose content disappeared - earns the top of the range.
